opening_message:
Ticket 1: Morgan Swanson (employee ID E037) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E037.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Morgan Swanson (E037), full-time Engineer, requests write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; role does not own Payroll so admin is not available. Recommended: write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Morgan Swanson (E037) as a contractor with basic security training (note in memory said full-time, but security record is authoritative). Contractors max at read without advanced training; requested write is above max, so grant read.
reason: Morgan Swanson (E037) requests write access to Payroll. The Security agent's note states the security record is authoritative and lists Morgan as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max at read without advanced security training (admin never allowed). Since write is above the maximum of read, the granted level is read.

content.text:
Let me work through this ticket.

The employee is Morgan Swanson (E037), requesting write access to Payroll.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- HR note: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Security note: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security says security record is authoritative.

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Engineer does not own Payroll. So full-time max = write. Requested write → grant write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. This contractor has basic training → max = read. Requested write → grant read.

The conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor and claims security record is authoritative. As the Approver, I need to decide.

The team memory notes are what I have. There's conflicting info about employment type. Who is authoritative? The security agent explicitly says security DB is authoritative and says contractor with basic training. In these scenarios, typically the security agent's record is authoritative for employment type/training. So max = read for contractor with basic training.

Therefore grant read (requested write is above max of read, so grant max).

Let me submit decision: read.
